tasks.process: User submits the idea
Identify the business domain and the capabilities needed. If confidence is low, use the generic core team and mark the domain as an assumption
Understand the idea, identify the starting point, give it a working name, assign the relevant agents
Extract explicit values with supporting quotes. Label inferred values separately, with rationale and confidence. Leave unknowns empty
Each slot owner writes a question for its slot. CSO ranks them, asks the top 3, and marks the rest as assumptions
User answers. The matching slots become confirmed. Maximum 2 clarification rounds; remaining unknowns are marked as assumptions
tasks.flow: After T5. CSO → User. Unfilled slots return to T5 (round 2 only)

tasks.process: Generate the Idea Brief draft from the collected context
tasks.flow: After T6. CSO uses the brief template

tasks.slots: The sections built from the slots each reviewer owns
tasks.process: Domain agents review their own sections. CQRO checks completeness, consistency, assumptions and risk
tasks.flow: After T7. CSO → Specialists → CQRO. A fail returns to T7

tasks.process: Strategic approval
tasks.flow: After T8. CSO → CEO. Changes return to T7

tasks.process: User reviews, then confirms or requests changes
tasks.flow: After T9. CEO → User. Changes return to T7 and repeat T8 and T9 before the User confirms again

tasks.process: Lock Idea Brief v1 and hand the confirmed context to Problem Discovery
Allocate: confirm the agent team from Phase 1, and add specialists if the problem needs them
tasks.flow: Starts after Phase 1 handoff. CSO → CEO if a new agent is needed

tasks.responsible: CSO + BA, with CCO, CMO, CFO
tasks.slots: problem, affected_users, pain_points, current_process, frequency, severity, business_impact
tasks.process: Fill: gather current-state facts from sources. Each fact gets a source, date, confidence and a provenance label (ai_estimated or sourced). Leave unknowns empty
Ask: each owner writes a question or evidence request for its slot. CSO ranks them and asks the top 3. The rest become assumptions
Ask: User answers, and can add their own evidence (interview notes, links, documents). Only the answered slots become confirmed. Maximum 2 rounds; remaining unknowns are marked as assumptions
tasks.flow: After T3. CSO → User. Unfilled slots return to T3 (round 2 only)

tasks.process: Generate: build the root causes behind the problem. Each cause links to a fact

tasks.input: The 8 input slots. problem and affected_users are mandatory
tasks.process: Generate: draft 2 to 3 framings of the problem statement. Block the draft unless problem and affected_users are explicit, inferred (with rationale) or confirmed. Other slots may be assumed, and appear in the statement as assumptions. CPO and CMO each comment on the options
tasks.flow: After T5. CSO → CPO, CMO. If blocked, CSO → User

tasks.process: Confirm: User picks one framing, and may edit it

tasks.responsible: CQRO + CDO, with CFO for business impact
tasks.input: Fact Sheet + Selected Problem Statement + User Evidence
tasks.slots: Evidence metadata for the 7 fact slots, and evidence links for root_causes
tasks.process: Review: check that each fact has evidence, check source quality and date, flag conflicts, and give an evidence score. Root causes and the problem statement must trace back to the facts they cite. Pass, or needs more evidence
tasks.flow: After T7. A fail for missing evidence returns to T3. A fail for the wrong framing returns to T6

tasks.process: Fill: label every unvalidated item as an assumption, ranked riskiest first

tasks.input: Fact Sheet + Root Cause Tree + Selected Problem Statement + Evidence Report + Assumption Register
tasks.process: Generate: draft the Problem Discovery document
tasks.flow: After T9. CSO uses the template

tasks.slots: The sections built from the slots each reviewer owns
tasks.process: Review: domain agents check their sections. CQRO checks completeness, consistency, evidence labels and risk
tasks.flow: After T10. A fail returns to T10

tasks.process: Strategic approval
tasks.flow: After T11. Changes return to T10

tasks.process: Confirm, or request changes
tasks.flow: After T12. Wording changes return to T10 and repeat T11 and T12. A different framing returns to T6

tasks.process: Handoff: lock the document and pass the confirmed context on

epics.name: Opportunity, Market & Customer Discovery
features: Opportunity Scoring (problem fit, market size, urgency, feasibility)
Market Sizing: TAM, SAM, SOM with editable assumptions
Source Quality, Date and Conflict Flags
Segment Prioritisation and Ideal Customer Profile (ICP)
Buyer vs User vs Decision-Maker Roles
Discovery Summary Export and Hand-off to later phases

tasks.process: Allocate: confirm the team, add specialists (market, regulation)
Fill: multi-query sourced research. Every source gets quality, date and conflict flags
Ask: add your own sources (links, documents). They are merged and flagged like the others
Refresh: re-run sources older than the age limit (default 90 days, configurable), or on demand
tasks.flow: Triggered by source age or by the User

tasks.input: Research Pack + Merged / Refreshed Source List
tasks.process: Generate: the cited market brief. Use refreshed sources when available
tasks.flow: After T2, T3 and T4 (if run)

tasks.process: Fill: size the market. Every assumption is editable
tasks.flow: After T5. User edits return here

tasks.process: Fill: growth and trends (CMO), regulation and compliance scan (CISO or COO), industry structure with PESTLE or Five Forces (CSO). The scan is a regulatory risk scan, not legal advice
tasks.flow: After T5. Runs parallel with T6

tasks.process: Fill: discover direct, indirect and substitute competitors
tasks.flow: After T5. Runs parallel with T6

tasks.process: Fill: profiles, feature comparison matrix, pricing table
Generate: SWOT and differentiation summary
Monitor: competitor change alerts (ongoing, not a one-time task)
Fill: editable segments, segment prioritisation and the ideal customer profile
tasks.flow: After T5. Runs parallel with T6

tasks.process: Generate: personas, JTBD and buyer, user and decision-maker roles. Each persona is labelled Synthetic. A persona built from User evidence names its evidence source instead

tasks.input: Segments, ICP, Personas, Market Sizing assumptions
tasks.process: Ask: review and edit. Only the downstream tasks that depend on an edited slot are re-run, not the whole phase
tasks.flow: After T6, T7, T10, T13. CSO → User

tasks.slots: market_gap, willingness_to_pay, opportunity_score (problem fit, market size, urgency, feasibility)
tasks.process: Fill: each role scores its own dimension. CPO scores problem fit, CFO market size and willingness to pay, CCO urgency, CTO feasibility, CSO the market gap
Generate: the Opportunity Signal with rationale: Go, Needs refinement or Weak. Also the strategic positioning and value hypothesis. A Weak signal suggests alternative problem framings
Fill: assumption register across the phase, riskiest first. Every item gets a confidence and provenance label
Generate: Discovery Summary, with export
Review: completeness, consistency, source quality, conflicts, labels. A fail returns to the task that produced it
Strategic approval of the summary and the signal
tasks.flow: After T19. Changes return to T18

tasks.process: Confirm: the Gate 1 User Decision: Go, Needs refinement or Stop
tasks.flow: After T20. CEO → User. Needs refinement returns to T14, then T15. Stop ends the journey and keeps all research. A Weak signal with a try-another-problem choice returns to Phase 2 T3

tasks.process: Handoff to Solution Discovery
Allocate: confirm the team, with more weight on CTO and CPO

tasks.input: Discovery Summary, problem_statement, root_causes, the Idea Brief’s idea
tasks.process: Generate: the User’s original idea becomes User Option 1, and the agents generate 2 to 4 more. Each option is labelled ai_written or user_written
Ask: add or edit your own options. User-written options are never dropped
Fill: link each option to the root causes it addresses. Flag root causes no option covers, and options that link to none
Fill: define the capabilities each option needs, in plain terms

tasks.input: Options, Map, Capabilities, Phase 2 and 3 evidence
tasks.process: Fill: score every option on root-cause coverage, feasibility, cost, user fit and market fit. Each score carries an evidence label. The same criteria apply to AI and User options. Unscored criteria are marked assumed
Generate: the Solution Discovery document, with the side-by-side comparison, a recommendation with rationale (not just a score), and open risks
Review: every option is linked to a root cause, evidence labels are present, criteria were applied equally to AI and User options. A fail returns to the task that produced the gap
Strategic approval
tasks.flow: After T8. Changes return to T7

tasks.process: Confirm: the User picks one option or a hybrid, including one the AI ranked lower. If so, the rationale and the extra risk are recorded
tasks.flow: After T9. CEO → User. A rejected shortlist returns to T3

tasks.process: Handoff to Business Model & Feasibility
Allocate: confirm the team, with more weight on CFO, CTO, COO and CISO

tasks.input: selected_solution, capabilities, Phase 3 icp, value_hypothesis, pricing_table
tasks.process: Fill: populate the 9 canvas blocks from earlier phases. Carried-over blocks keep their source. Unknown blocks stay empty
Ask: each owner writes a question for its block. CSO ranks them and asks the top 3. The rest become assumptions
Ask: User answers. Only the answered blocks become confirmed. Maximum 2 rounds
tasks.flow: After T3. Unfilled blocks return to T3 (round 2 only)

tasks.process: Ask: prepare the financial input request: price, unit cost, expected volume, fixed costs, funding available. Sourced reference ranges may be shown beside each field, labelled sourced, and are never auto-filled
Ask: User provides the figures. Each one is labelled user_provided. Skipped fields stay empty
Generate: unit economics, break-even and scenarios, calculated by formulas from user_provided figures only. If inputs are missing, produce a qualitative case and state that no figures were computed

tasks.input: Canvas, Phase 3 regulatory_risks, Phase 3 assumption register
tasks.process: Fill: risks by category (market, technical, financial, operational, regulatory, security), each with likelihood, impact and a mitigation. Link each to the assumption it comes from
tasks.flow: After T4. Runs parallel with T7

tasks.input: Canvas, Business Case, Risk Register, capabilities
tasks.process: Fill: technical, operational and financial feasibility, with effort and time ranges labelled ai_estimated. The verdict is Feasible, Feasible with conditions or Not feasible, with rationale. Financial feasibility uses only user_provided figures
Generate: the Business Model & Feasibility document

Review: no financial figure is without a user_provided label, the canvas is consistent with Phases 3 and 4, every risk is linked, and the feasibility basis is stated. A fail returns to the task that produced the gap
Strategic approval
tasks.flow: After T11. Changes return to T10

tasks.process: Confirm: single confirmation for the whole phase (canvas, financials, business case, risks, feasibility), or request changes
tasks.flow: After T12. Changes return to the producing task and repeat T11 and T12

tasks.process: Handoff to Product Definition

tasks.input: Confirmed Business Model & Feasibility doc + Context
tasks.process: Allocate: confirm the team, with more weight on CPO, CXO and CTO

tasks.input: Phase 3 personas, icp, buyer_roles, Phase 1 target_users
tasks.process: Fill: carry over and refine the personas into primary and secondary product users. Each is linked to its persona and keeps its label (Synthetic or evidence source)
Fill: outcome goals, each traced to expected_outcome. Success metrics with baseline, target and measurement method. Targets are proposals and stay assumed until the User confirms

tasks.input: selected_solution, capabilities, Phase 1 constraints, feasibility, financial_inputs
tasks.process: Generate: in scope, out of scope and the MVP boundary. Every exclusion states its reason

tasks.input: Gaps in users, outcomes, metrics and scope
tasks.process: Ask: each owner writes a question for its slot. CPO ranks them and asks the top 3. The rest become assumptions
Ask: User answers. Only the answered slots become confirmed. Maximum 2 rounds
tasks.flow: After T5. Unfilled slots return to T5 (round 2 only)

tasks.process: Fill: define the product features. Each links to a capability and a root cause, with a priority (must, should, could). Flag capabilities with no feature and features with no capability
Generate: a journey per product user and key goal. Each has steps, touchpoints, the pain points it removes and the features used
Fill: 3 to 7 UX principles, each with a rationale tied to a user, a journey or a constraint
Generate: the Product Definition document

Review the traceability chain: every feature links to a capability and a root cause, every outcome goal links to expected_outcome, every journey links to a product user, and scope respects constraints and feasibility. Metrics must be measurable. A fail returns to the task that produced the gap
Strategic approval
tasks.flow: After T11. Changes return to T10

tasks.process: Confirm, or request changes
tasks.flow: After T12. Wording changes return to T10 and repeat T11 and T12. Scope changes return to T4

tasks.process: Handoff to the Requirement Register

tasks.input: Confirmed Product Definition doc + all earlier phase documents
tasks.process: Allocate: confirm the team, with more weight on CTO, CISO, CDO and CPO

tasks.input: constraints, Phase 3 market slots, Phase 5 business_model_canvas, business_case, risks
tasks.process: Fill: business requirements. Each is one statement with a priority, an acceptance criterion and a link to its source slot
Fill: user requirements (a [user] can [goal] so that [outcome]), each linked to a journey step
tasks.flow: After T1. Runs parallel with T2

tasks.process: Fill: functional requirements, each linked to a product feature and a user requirement, with acceptance criteria
Fill: for each AI feature: accuracy target, data needs, human oversight, transparency and fallback. Marked not applicable if the product uses no AI. Targets are proposals
tasks.flow: After T4. Runs parallel with T6

tasks.process: Fill: performance, security, privacy, compliance, availability, scalability, accessibility and usability requirements. Each has a measurable target that stays assumed until confirmed
tasks.flow: After T4. Runs parallel with T5

tasks.process: Fill: the system assigns stable IDs (BR, UR, FR, AIR, NFR) and links each requirement to its source and to related requirements. Flag requirements with no source, and sources (features, capabilities, risks) with no requirement
Fill: dependencies, conflicts and sequencing between requirements. Flag circular dependencies and conflicting pairs
Review: each requirement is atomic, testable, unambiguous, measurable, prioritised and traceable. Pass or fail per requirement
tasks.flow: After T8. A fail returns to the writer of that requirement

tasks.input: Questions on failed requirements, grouped by theme
tasks.process: Ask: User resolves the open questions. Limit per round to be set. Maximum 2 rounds; unresolved items stay open and cannot be baselined
tasks.flow: After T9. CSO → User. Answers return to T9

tasks.process: Generate: the Requirement Register, one table with ID, type, priority, source, acceptance criterion and status
Review: coverage of every Product Definition feature, duplicates, consistency, dependency conflicts. A fail returns to the writer
Strategic approval
tasks.flow: After T12. Changes return to T11

tasks.process: Confirm: bulk approval by group (business, user, functional, AI, non-functional) or all at once. Exceptions are sent back or left open
tasks.flow: After T13. Exceptions return to the writer and repeat T9

tasks.process: Publish: lock the approved requirements as Baseline v1 with frozen IDs. Later edits go through Change Management
Allocate: confirm the team and the document set (default: BRD, PRD, SRS, MRD, FRS)

tasks.input: Baseline (business requirements), Phase 1 and Phase 5 documents
tasks.process: Generate: the BRD from the baseline, citing every requirement ID

tasks.input: Baseline (business requirements), Phase 3 market, competitor and segment slots
tasks.process: Generate: the MRD
tasks.flow: After T1. Runs parallel with T2

tasks.input: Baseline (user and functional requirements), Phase 6 slots
tasks.process: Generate: the PRD
tasks.flow: After T1. Runs parallel with T2

tasks.process: Generate: the SRS
tasks.flow: After T1. Runs parallel with T2

tasks.process: Generate: the FRS. For each function: inputs, outputs, rules, error cases and acceptance criteria
tasks.flow: After T1. Runs parallel with T2

tasks.process: Check: IDs resolve, every baseline requirement appears in the documents it belongs to, no contradictory statements, terms are used the same way, every document cites Baseline v1. Issues are blocking or warning
tasks.flow: After T2 to T6. A blocking issue returns to the owner of that document (maximum 2 loops)

tasks.process: Review: each document is complete against its template, readable and free of unflagged risk. A fail returns to the owner
Strategic approval of the set
tasks.flow: After T8. Changes return to the owner and repeat T7 and T8

tasks.process: Confirm: approve the set as a whole, or request changes to one document
tasks.flow: After T9. A change request returns to that document's owner and repeats T7 to T9

tasks.input: Approved Documents + Baseline + Matrix + Assumption Register
tasks.process: Assemble the Handoff Package: documents, baseline, traceability matrix, open assumptions, decision log, version stamps, and exports
Handoff to the next stage. From here Change Management watches the baseline

epics.name: Change Management
epics.mappingTitle: Change Management (runs when a change happens)

tasks.input: Edits to confirmed slots or documents, stale sources, new evidence, competitor alerts
tasks.process: Detect: watch for changes and record each as a Change Event. Some of this exists in the prototype: an edit to a confirmed document is detected
Reopen: reopen the item and record the reason, requester and scope. A change proposed by an agent needs the User's acceptance
Mark out of date: flag every dependent slot and document as out of date, and pause their approvals. Some of this exists in the prototype

tasks.responsible: CSO + CPO, CTO, CFO and the owners of affected slots
tasks.process: Analyse impact: what changes, severity (minor or major), effort, cost, risk, and the baseline version affected. Recommend apply, defer or reject
Decide: apply, defer or reject the change. Major changes also need the CEO's approval
tasks.flow: After T4. Defer or reject closes the request

tasks.responsible: Owner agents, guided by the Orchestrator
tasks.process: Guided update: the owners update the affected items in dependency order. Each update shows a before-and-after difference. The User is asked only where needed
Review: the consistency and traceability checks run again on what changed
tasks.flow: After T6. A fail returns to T6

tasks.process: Re-confirm: the User re-confirms only the affected items. Unaffected items stay confirmed. Major changes also need the CEO
Version and close: publish the new baseline version, record who changed what, why and under which request, and add a comparison with the previous version. Update the Handoff Package

slots.supporting: the User, or the agent that proposed it

epics.name: Skill Integration
epics.mappingTitle: Skill Integration (platform layer, used by every step)
features: Skill and KB Catalog (list from the KB service; browse by phase and role)
Skill Recommendation for the current step
Enable / Disable per project and per step
Version Pinning per project (use a chosen version, switch back to an earlier one)
Skill Permissions (who can enable a skill in a project)
Service Connection with connection test and status
KB Grounding (use KB content in a step and show the cited sources)
Skill Usage Log (which skill shaped which output)
Skill Availability Status (shows if a skill is retired or unavailable)

tasks.input: KB service details entered in secure settings, never in chat or documents
tasks.process: Connect the KB service, run a connection test and show the status (connected, failing, unavailable). Retry on demand
tasks.flow: Starts at project setup. CDO → Orchestrator

tasks.process: Fetch the skill and KB catalog from the KB service. Browse by phase and role. Each entry shows version and status

tasks.input: Catalog + current phase, step and slots
tasks.process: Recommend skills for the current step, ranked, each with a reason tied to the phase, role or slot. A recommendation never enables anything
tasks.flow: After T2. Runs at the start of each step

tasks.input: A selected skill + a sample from the current step
tasks.process: Preview: run the skill on the sample and show its effect, labelled Preview. Nothing is saved to project documents
Configure tone, depth and output format, per skill, project or step
Check the User's role may enable this skill in this project. If not, send an approval request to the project owner
Enable or disable the skill for the project or for one step
Pin a chosen version for the project. Switching back to an earlier version is allowed. A switch is a change event, and outputs shaped by the old version are flagged
tasks.flow: After T7. A switch triggers Change Management T1

tasks.input: Enabled Skill Set for the task
tasks.process: At the start of each task, resolve the skills for this project, step and agent. Apply the fallback and conflict order
tasks.flow: Before every task in every phase

tasks.process: Use KB content in the step. Every passage used is cited (title, version, date, link). KB claims without a citation are flagged, and conflicting sources are flagged
tasks.flow: After T9. Inside the task that uses it

tasks.input: Every task that used a skill
tasks.process: Record which skill and version, with which configuration, shaped which output (document and section), by which agent, and when
Detect a retired or unavailable skill or a KB outage. Mark its status, list the outputs it shaped, apply the fallback, and notify the User
tasks.flow: Continuous. A retirement triggers Change Management T1

tasks.input: Outputs that used a skill + Usage Log
tasks.process: Review: citations are present, the configuration was respected, the usage log is complete, and no skill outside the enabled set was used

epics.name: C-Suite Integration
epics.mappingTitle: C-Suite Integration (human executive review, applied at each phase gate)
features: Executive Role Selection (which roles review a project)
Executive Summary View per phase (one page)
Approve / Request Changes / Reject at gates
Solution Outcomes View (expected outcomes against success measures and KPIs)
AI Challenge Mode (AI questions assumptions from each role's view, clearly labelled)
Notifications for review requests and decisions

tasks.process: Select which executive roles review this project and which people hold them. The CSO suggests defaults. Mark which roles are required at each gate
Define each role's lens per phase (for example CFO: financials, CTO: feasibility, CISO: security)
Draft a validation checklist per role, per phase
Generate a one-page Executive Summary for the phase, with each role's lens highlights
tasks.flow: After each phase's CEO approval step

tasks.process: Create one review request per required role, assign the person, attach the checklist and due date
AI Challenge Mode (optional): each role agent questions the assumptions from its role's view. Every item is labelled AI challenge and can be dismissed
tasks.flow: After T4. Runs parallel with T5

tasks.input: Executive Summary + document + Checklist + Challenge Questions
tasks.process: Review: add comments and questions on items, tick the checklist, then Approve, Request changes or Reject
Answer questions and resolve comments. Changes return to the task that produced the item
tasks.flow: After T7. Changes return to the phase's generating task

tasks.process: Combine the decisions: all required roles Approve, the gate can pass. Any Request changes, rework. Any Reject, the gate stops
Record decision, reason, who and when. Append only

tasks.input: Risks and assumptions from all phases
tasks.process: Roll up the risks of all phases into one register with owner, severity, status and source
tasks.flow: After each phase, kept in sync

tasks.process: Show expected outcomes against success measures and KPIs, with status and the source of each target
tasks.flow: After Product Definition, updated after each change

tasks.process: Show the review status by phase and role (requested, in review, approved, changes requested, rejected, overdue)
Notify on review requests, comments, mentions and decisions

tasks.input: Approved documents, Executive Summaries, Risk Register, Outcomes View, Decision Log
tasks.process: Generate the Board-Ready Brief for export as PDF or slides. CQRO reviews it. The User approves before export
tasks.flow: On request, after Gate 1 or any later gate

tasks.process: Allocate: confirm the team, with more weight on CTO, CISO, CDO and COO

tasks.input: functional_requirements, ai_requirements, nonfunctional_requirements, constraints, feasibility, regulatory_risks
tasks.process: Fill: gather the inputs the architecture must satisfy and show them with their requirement IDs
Confirm the inputs, and add constraints (existing systems, hosting, team skills, budget). Only added items become confirmed
Generate 2 to 3 candidate patterns and score them against the non-functional requirements, cost and team skills, with evidence labels. Recommend one
Confirm: choose a pattern, or a different one with the rationale recorded
Fill: identify the layers and the components in each, every one linked to requirement IDs. Flag requirements with no component and components with no requirement
Fill: map dependencies, data flows and external services. Flag circular dependencies and single points of failure
Generate: one Architecture Decision Record per significant decision, with context, options, decision, consequences, status and linked requirement IDs
Generate: the Solution Architecture document: overview, layer view, component catalog, dependency map, data and security views, and a traceability table to requirement IDs
Review: every non-functional requirement is addressed, security and data views are complete, traceability is complete, ADRs are consistent with the SRS. A fail returns to the producing task
Strategic approval
tasks.flow: After T10. Changes return to T9

tasks.process: Confirm, or request changes
tasks.flow: After T11. Wording changes return to T9 and repeat T10 and T11. A different pattern returns to T4

tasks.process: Publish Architecture Baseline v1, add it to the Handoff Package as a new version, and hand off

tasks.input: Architecture Baseline v1 (layers and components), functional_requirements
tasks.process: Fill: identify the services from the architecture components, each with its responsibility and the requirement IDs it serves
Fill: define how services interact (calls, events, data exchanged) and draw the main system flows and sequence diagrams
tasks.output: Interaction Map + Flow and Sequence Diagrams

tasks.input: Selected architecture pattern, nonfunctional_requirements, constraints, financial_inputs
tasks.process: Fill: recommend a stack per layer with alternatives and reasons, scored against non-functional requirements, cost and team skills. This is a recommendation only. 21.2 freezes it
Generate: the HLD document, with a traceability table to requirement IDs
Review: every service traces to a component and a requirement, flows are complete, stack choices are justified. A fail returns to the producing task
Fill: list every AI use case from the AI requirements, identify the agents needed and classify them (for example assistant, workflow, reviewer, tool-using). Not applicable if the product uses no AI
Fill: design each AI workflow step by step and how the agents coordinate (handoffs, shared context, who decides)
Fill: state what each workflow needs from a model (quality, latency, privacy), shortlist models, design routing between them, and estimate cost with ai_estimated labels
Fill: design the prompt structure, which skills apply, the tools and functions agents may call, where knowledge comes from, and how memory is kept and limited
Fill: define guardrails and human-oversight points, the test sets and pass criteria for evaluating AI output, and what is logged and monitored
Generate: the AI Solution Design document
Review: every AI requirement is addressed, guardrails cover the identified risks, evaluation is measurable. A fail returns to the producing task
Fill: extract what must connect to what (SaaS tools, external APIs, internal services) and map the dependencies between integrations
Fill: design each SaaS and API integration (direction, data, trigger) and each webhook (events, payload, delivery, retries)
Fill: choose the authentication for each integration (no secrets in documents) and map fields between our data model and each external API
Fill: define what happens on failure (retry, back-off, fallback, alert) and how each external rate limit is respected
Generate: the Integration Design document
Review: every integration requirement is addressed, authentication and error handling are defined for each integration, no secrets appear in the document. A fail returns to the producing task
Fill: extract what data the product must store and query, identify the entities with their attributes, and map the relationships between them
tasks.output: Data Requirements + Entity List + Relationship Map

tasks.process: Generate: the ER model and the relational schema (tables, keys, constraints, indexes)

tasks.input: Data Requirements, ai_requirements, AI Solution Design if applicable
tasks.process: Fill: design document stores, vector stores (only if AI search or memory needs them) and file or data-lake storage. Each is marked not applicable if unused
Fill: design the migration from any existing data, and the retention and deletion rules per entity, checked against the regulatory risks
Generate: the Database Design document
Review: every entity traces to a requirement, schemas match the API and AI designs, retention meets the regulatory risks. A fail returns to the producing task
Fill: extract the operations the API must offer, per consumer (own front end, partners, integrations)
Generate: the REST design, the GraphQL design where it applies, and the endpoint list (method, path, purpose, requirement ID)
Generate: the request and response schemas for each endpoint, and one consistent error contract

tasks.input: Endpoint List, authentication and authorization design from 18.2
tasks.process: Fill: state who may call each endpoint and how they authenticate, taken from the Security design, plus the versioning and deprecation rules
Generate: the API documentation (for example an OpenAPI specification) directly from the endpoints and schemas, never written separately
Review: every endpoint traces to a requirement, schemas match the database design, every endpoint has an access rule, errors follow the contract. A fail returns to the producing task
Fill: analyse the security requirements and model threats per component and data flow (assets, actors, threats, mitigations), ranked by severity
Fill: design how users and services authenticate, what each role may do, and how identities and access are managed (roles, least privilege, session rules)
Fill: design encryption in transit and at rest, how secrets and credentials are stored and rotated (never in documents), and the API protections
tasks.output: Encryption, Secrets and API Security Design

tasks.input: Threat Model, AI Solution Design if applicable
tasks.process: Fill: design protections for AI features: treat all retrieved and user text as data, not instructions; limit tool permissions; stop sensitive data leaking through prompts, logs or outputs. Not applicable if no AI
Fill: define what is logged (who, what, when), retention and tamper protection, and map each compliance obligation to a control. This is a control mapping, not legal advice
Generate: the Security Design document
Review: every security requirement and threat has a control, secret-handling rules are stated, the compliance map is complete. A fail returns to the producing task
Fill: extract availability, scale, region, budget and compliance needs, and design the cloud architecture (provider, regions, main services)

tasks.slots: network_architecture, compute_architecture, container_architecture, storage_architecture, database_infrastructure, queue_event_architecture
tasks.process: Fill: design the network, compute, containers, storage, database hosting, and queues or events
Fill: design the build and release pipeline and the environments (development, test, production), with promotion rules
Fill: design infrastructure scaling rules and limits, backup, recovery time and recovery point objectives, and the failover plan, with cost noted
Generate: the Infrastructure Design document
Review: availability and recovery targets are met by the design, cost is noted, security controls are reflected. A fail returns to the producing task

slots.slot: network_architecture, compute_architecture, container_architecture, storage_architecture, database_infrastructure, queue_event_architecture

tasks.process: Fill: break each service into modules, define the classes or service units, and the interfaces between them
Fill: detail each workflow, draw sequence diagrams at class level, and write the business rules in plain form
Fill: define input validation rules, error handling per layer, and the dependencies between modules (no cycles)
Generate: the LLD document
Review: every module traces to a service and a requirement, workflows match the user journeys, error handling matches the API error contract. A fail returns to the producing task

tasks.input: hld_stack_recommendation, constraints, team skills (from the User)
